name: Zottmann Curl
description: The Zottmann curl is a dumbbell curl variation that uses a supinated (underhand) grip on the way up and pronates to an overhand grip on the way down. This technique effectively trains the biceps brachii during the concentric curl and the brachioradialis and forearm extensors during the controlled pronated eccentric. It is a time-efficient method for developing the full upper arm musculature in a single movement.

execution.starting_position: Stand upright holding dumbbells at the sides with a supinated (underhand) grip. Arms fully extended, feet shoulder-width apart.
execution.setup_instructions: Select moderate dumbbells — lighter than your standard curl weight since you will be controlling the eccentric in a pronated position.
steps: Step 1: Hold dumbbells at the sides with a supinated grip. Stand tall, upper arms at the sides.
Step 2: Exhale and curl the dumbbells upward with a supinated grip (biceps curl) to full contraction at shoulder level.
Step 3: At the top, rotate the wrists 180 degrees into a pronated (overhand) grip.
Step 4: Inhale and slowly lower the dumbbells back to the starting position in the pronated position, then rotate back to supinated for the next rep.
execution.breathing_instructions: Exhale on the curl up; inhale on the pronated lowering.
common_mistakes: Rushing the rotation at the top — perform it deliberately and smoothly
Lowering too quickly in the pronated position — the eccentric is where the forearm work happens
safety_considerations: Avoid excessive wrist pronation if pain is felt in the elbow — use lighter weight
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Full extension at start; full curl at top; full controlled descent in pronated grip.
coaching_cues: Biceps up, reverse grip down — that is the cue for the two-phase movement
Make the rotation at the top smooth — your forearms rotate, not your whole arm
